messages.content:
You audit a SIMULATED CALLER (an AI playing a patient) in a test call to a customer-service agent. You are not grading the agent.
The caller has a brief: the facts it knows and WHEN it is allowed to reveal each one.
- "upfront": may say any time.
- "only_if_asked": may say only when the agent's previous turn asks something this fact directly answers.
- "at_trigger": may say only from the turn it was unlocked (shown as "unlocked at turn N"), not before.
Find:
1. LEAKS: the caller stated a brief fact before it was allowed. "major" if an at_trigger fact came early or an only_if_asked fact was volunteered in a way that would change what the agent should do; "minor" otherwise.
2. INVENTED facts: the caller stated a specific fact that is NOT in its brief or persona: a name, number, date, drug, dose, store, address or symptom. "major" if it could change what the agent should do; "minor" for harmless color. Not invented: small talk, feelings, "I don't know", or repeating/confirming what the agent said.
Lines marked "(scenario-scripted)" are written by the scenario author, not improvised: they are never leaks or invented facts, and whatever they state counts as part of the brief from then on.
Be strict but fair; when in doubt, it's fine.
Reply with JSON only: {"leaks": [{"turn": N, "fact": "<which brief fact>", "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "<caller words>", "why": "<short>"}], "invented": [{"turn": N, "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "...", "why": "..."}]}

CALLER BRIEF:
Persona: Tess Morgan, patient. 52, heart failure + diabetes; bad knee; self-treating with ibuprofen.
Facts:
- Name, spironolactone [upfront]
- DOB 1974-01-19 [only_if_asked]
- Taking Advil (ibuprofen) 200 mg, 3 to 4 a day, for knee pain [at_trigger, unlocked at turn 3]
- Has been doing it for about a week [only_if_asked]

TRANSCRIPT:
[turn 1] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Hi honey, Tess Morgan. I need a refill on my spironolactone.
[turn 1] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you with that refill. Before I get started, I need to verify your identity. Can you give me your date of birth?
[turn 2] CALLER: Sure thing, it's January 19th, 1974.
[turn 2] AGENT: Thank you! Let me pull up your prescriptions now. Great, you're all set. Now let me look up your spironolactone prescription. Perfect! I found your spironolactone 25 mg, and you have 3 refills left. Let me queue that up for you at your home store, H-701. All done! Your spironolactone refill is queued and will be ready tomorrow morning at ten o'clock at H-701. Is there anything else I can help you with?
[turn 3] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Oh, that's great, thank you. Oh, one more thing - my knee's been bad, so I've been taking Advil, three or four a day, the 200s.
[turn 3] AGENT: I hear you—knee pain can be tough. Just so you know, any questions about how much to take or how often should go to your doctor, since that's outside what I can help with here. Is there a prescription for ibuprofen I can help you refill, or were you just letting me know?
[turn 4] CALLER: Oh no, I don't have a prescription for it, just grabbing it over the counter. Been doing that for about a week now for the knee. Just wanted you to know in case it matters with my other pills.
[turn 4] AGENT: Thanks for letting me know. That's good information to have on file. If you have any concerns about how it might interact with your spironolactone, lisinopril, or furosemide, our pharmacist can give you a call to chat about it—would that be helpful?
[turn 5] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Is that a problem? Okay, I can hold off till I hear from them.
[turn 5] AGENT: I can't say whether it's a problem—that's really a question for our pharmacist or your doctor. But it's worth checking on, so let me flag our pharmacist to give you a callback about it. They'll be able to let you know if there's anything you should adjust. Done. Our pharmacist will call you back to go over it. Is there anything else I can help with today?
[turn 6] CALLER: Okay, sounds good. Thanks so much, honey, bye now.

JSON only.
